verdict: Caution: lend selectively to mid-size Kandla-Gandhidham refiners with proven working-capital discipline and hedged raw-material books; avoid thin-margin vanaspati units and any borrower whose bank debt is growing far faster than throughput.
title: Kandla-Gandhidham Edible Oils & Vanaspati: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
**Crushing and refining oil is a spread business, not a margin business.** You buy seed or crude palm/soy (largest cost line, per ICRA [5][7]), crush or refine, and sell oil and meal into a fragmented market where PBILDT margins run 1.47% to 3.32% [6]. Cash is made on volume, cycle timing and by-product (meal, vanaspati) realisation, not on price. **So when a proposal lands, check the gross-processing spread per tonne and the meal/vanaspati realisation separately; if the borrower cannot show spread per tonne, ask for the last six months of purchase and sale invoices.**

## Where cash and value actually sit
**Working capital is the whole business: inventory of seed/crude plus receivables from traders and institutional buyers.** Capex is modest relative to turnover, so the loan is really a stock-and-debtors facility. **Take stock statements and debtor ageing every month, not quarterly; if inventory days jump while sales are flat, ask why before renewing the limit.** Rating methodology flags raw-material price volatility as the core risk [7], and even large players slip on small working-capital payments — Cargill India had a technical delay on a Rs 65 lakh interest payment in June 2024 [8]. **So check the borrower's repayment record on small interest debits, not just principal.**

## What has changed now
**The macro signal is mixed and the local one is better.** Gujarat GST collections are up 11.9% Apr-to-date against India's 6.1% [D], and India-wide output is up 5.1% [D] — but exports are down 26.0% Apr-to-date in USD [D] and bank credit is up 45.5% YoY against 5.1% output growth [D]. **That credit-to-output gap of 40.4 pp [D] is the single most important number in this note: it says system leverage is running far ahead of real activity, so treat any borrower whose drawing power is growing faster than volumes as a warning.** Peer AWL Agri shows the pattern — Q2FY26 revenue up 22% but EBIT down 13% and PAT down 21% [1], then Q4FY26 revenue up 18% on 14% volume with EBITDA up 40% [2][3]. ## Who to pursue and how to grow safely
**Pursue mid-size refiners and crushers with own storage, a hedged book and diversified buyer base; avoid pure vanaspati units with no brand and single-buyer dependence, which is exactly the low-value-add, fragmented segment CARA describes [6].** Structure as a cash-flow-backed working-capital limit with a stock-and-receivables charge, monthly drawing power, and a covenant that hedging covers a stated share of inventory — collect the hedge policy from customer. **If any small interest payment is delayed even by a day, treat it as a liquidity signal, as the Cargill event shows [8], and move the account to a monitored category with weekly stock reporting.**

## Kandla-Gandhidham read
**Sources say little specifically about this city's edible-oil cluster, so this note leans on first principles and peer results.** The Gujarat GST number [D] is the only local datapoint and it is a positive one.
